question.text: An organ pipe <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long is open at both ends. The speed of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>360</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The frequency of the second harmonic is _<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
The formula for the frequency in an open organ pipe is 

f=nv2L

Since, it is a second harmonic, n=2

The frequency of the second harmonic becomes f=2v2L=vL

The data given is 

L=0.4 mv=360 m s-1

Substituting the values in the frequency formula

f=360 m s-10.4 m=900 Hz
